texts: It needs to be stated upfront that I'm one of the top ten fractalists who specializes in fractal flowers, possibly top three, with more than a hundred published designs in the wild. That's excluding private designs that I've shared with patrons, my inner circle, or never even left the design stage to be rendered. Do not consider the below list to be representative... even less so to be comprehensive.

content.text:
## The Heart of Winter

_aka, "The Black Dahlia"_

Even more mandala-like and dahlia-like than her sister, "[Bloom of Fire](bloom-of-fire)", the bokeh in "The Heart of Winter" can just as easily be falling, crystalline snowflakes that adorn her petals. I had to wait two years between the two fractal flowers for technology to improve, since "Bloom of Fire" took eleven days to render. Even with the massive upgrades in that time, this fractal flower took a little over three days to finish rendering. Even then, the intense rendering process almost caused it to fail before it could see the light of day. The result is a much more ethereal and haunting bloom than her sister, yet with the very same crystalline siren's call found only in snowflakes.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/29056161)\]

## Lotus Lily Pads

You might notice the same spiral stamen technique (coth\_spiral + blur) that my "[Filigree Floranocte](filigree-floranocte)" fractal flower features. With the lotus, however, I wanted a nearly bioluminescent look to her, not too dissimilar to flora on the moon of Pandora, leading to a series of fractal flowers that I created using glowing blue and green colors. I'll include the other star-showing from this same series and technique here below.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/26841863)\]

## Invidian Garden

_aka, "Stargazer Lilies"_

This fractal flower followed immediately after "Lotus Lily Pads" in the same series, highlighting more the colors and a deeper gradient in exchange for some of the luminescence found in her sister. Her title also gives away one of the inspirations for the color palette. If they featured a matte, light gray in the flowers, they would be a spot-on match with the Invid extraterrestrial fleet that attacks the planet Earth in the original anime series "Robotech" -- almost spot for spot. This final design nearly perfectly matches the growth pattern and form of stargazer lilies, giving her the nickname that lasts even to this day.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/26975849)\]

## Heart of Autumn _aka, "Apoptosis: The Fractal Geometry of Falling Leaves"_ When I first published these fractal leaves for sale I did so under the name "Apoptosis" with no SEO. At that time, I was interested in sells and and promoting my visual arts. It's a lesson that I should have learned previously, as it was almost as bad marketing as Commodore's marketing for the Amiga 9000, the absolute best personal computer gaming system that no one ever heard of. The Amiga 9000 has thousands of colors, could be carried just as a keyboard and plugged into a monitor anywhere, with hundreds of games ready to play on it. It also supported four-channel stereo audio. This is in the 80s, nearly a decade ahead of the Mac and Windows having anything near to the same capabilities. Commodore's marketing was so horrid that they ended up burying it in an unmarked grave near discarded Atari cartridges. But I remember. _Lemmings_, _Settlers_, _Syndicate_, just to name a few. That last game was my introduction to the idea that games could be incredibly and painfully -- very much graphically -- violent! Andy Warhol never gave up his 9000, then Hollywood created The Video Toaster using the system for early movies like "Lawnmower Man" and series like "Babylon 5". But it was too late. These legacy systems were the only ones that would ever be produced. It had already been buried. Hence why to-this-day, more than 90% of my designs found on stores have SEO titles in place and available for purchase. Facts: The word "apoptosis" comes from the ancient Greeks, and was used to describe the falling of leaves from trees… as well as the falling of petals from flowers. It is used, now, in modern medicine to describe the difference between a body-cell that dies naturally and intentionally... and a cell that dies from injury or poison... to describe the leaves of our own bodies falling away from us. \[[Apoptosis on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23496370)\]

## Anemone Mine

_aka, "Seventh Anemone"_

This one goes out to _you_, Geda! And to everyone else, Geda still wears this design as earrings to this very day. However, you won't find those earrings online, so [contact me](contact) if you're interested and describe your preferred style. Technically, this is not the most popular version of this design, although it has plenty of fans and buyers [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/28598267). The real big hit is the glowing neon-green version in blue crystalline water, the same that appears as the album cover for "PORN" by First 5 Frets... aka, "The Flower of the Long Sleep" (for those who know their Atlantean history). You'll find the reaper flower herself [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23116372). Again, custom designs are available and I love jamming out over new and unique ideas.

At last shall find you by the river-brink,  
And, offering his Cup, invite your Soul  
Forth to your Lips to quaff -- you shall not shrink!</font>_

~**Edward Fitzgerald's** _"Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam"_

\[[UV Anemone on Redubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/28598267)\] \[[Blue-Green Anemone on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23116372)\]

## Faerie Ferns

_dedicated to my semi-incestuous little sister, 4C1D F43R13!_

When I first purchased a license to Chaotica, beginning the slow migration from Apophysis, this was the very first fractal that I worked on. The pre-transforms with the "blur" function lend themselves to this incredible depth-of-field effect that you see here in this design. My little sister Faerie refuses to call herself a photographer, but one thing that stands out for me in her photography is her incredible use of DoF (long before it was standard on phones). Well, that and her way of capturing the essence of a person in a portrait shot. Except for herself. She's sheit at self-portraits and needs to be banned from even fucking trying.

When I return to the world of fractal design, it will be ferns and depth-of-field effects like this that I first focus on. I give it an 80% chance that it plays out that way, so betting odds are good.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/26063326)\] \[[Alternate on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/26534636)\]

## Lotus Pearls

_aka, "The Pink Dahlia"_

This isn't the first time that one of my pearlescent designs was a big hit, as that record goes to my "[Mother of Pearl](mother-of-pearl)" design itself which is in my top-five-of-all-time list. BUT! The "Lotus Pearls" comes in second in those regards, with the first week being a rush of sales big enough to raise my eyebrows at. My any of my pearl designs, there doesn't seem to be a middle-ground. They either skyrocket or they never get off the launchpad. In this case, I can see the fuel train for the design leading out of the solar system. I have plans to return to the concept in the future and add quite a few more 3D elements to really bring a different, offspring of this one into life in a completely different way.

As I write this, I just got word from my brother Zero that HF-1 took his own life . . and now the world is a darker place without our wrecking ball of a badass.

Dropping the link for this one and pouring a drink in his honor.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/26816806)\]

## India Inferno

My final of the three butterfly separation fractal flowers that I ever created, although with this one, I ended up rendering as black and white then coloring as three separate designs. It's a technique that I adopted after my friend Charlie in Washington DC told me that he was colorblind and had trouble making out the details in my images. Ever since then, I've designed completely in black and white, focusing on the luminescent depth of the design itself. Only afterward, as the final step, do I approach how it will be colored. In this case, I put all three designs in front of my patrons to vote on. "India Inferno" as you see here on the right won out by a large margin.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/28370566)\]

## Daffodil Meadow

Technically, this should be catalogued alongside "[Heart of the Rose](heart-of-the-rose)" and "[Mother of Pearl](mother-of-pearl)" as a Mandelbrot fractal. It's long-since strayed from those roots to grow wild into the design you now see before you. So... _I won't tell if you won't tell. Shhhhhh!_ I first fell in love with daffodils in France. In spring, they pop up in the cement islands between traffic, as well as alongside the sidewalks, and then anywhere that allows them to take root and explode. In the design, they are more flat than their Terran counterparts, but still carry that explosive star-like yellow... and all bursting forth from the deep greens around them. They've since become one of my top ten most-popular fractal flowers.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/28642718)\]

## Angel Fire Orchids

This design was inspired after visiting Marché aux Fleurs in Paris, France during the autumnal equinox in 2016. You can see the photo that I took of Moth Orchids (Phalaenopsis) here below this image. While the colors at Marché aux Fleurs cannot be overstated nor praised highly enough, it's the incredible hypnotic scents that reaches you first... even when more than a block away. At that point, you no longer need a map. You can follow your nose. One shop after another, one lane after another, each adorned with florists on every side -- it's a welcome full-on assault on the senses.

And we wouldn't have it any other way.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/28692615)\]

content.text:
## Origami Orchid

_aka, "Edelweiss"_

Another from my orchids, this time in turquoise, violet, and blue and with much thicker spirals. I also focused heavily on the "jewel bud" at the center, with another orchid taking form inside it as if we could see inside the seed itself to peer into the true treasures of the orchid herself -- the children that she sends into the world to meet us. Odd thing here, which is that I myself absolutely love this one, but I think in all its time online it's never made a single sale. No complaints really, as I love her just like this and wouldn't change anything about the design... yet it remains a curioso that draws me back for study to understand the minds and hearts of others.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/31887584)\]

## By Any Other Name

_aka, "Thorn"_

I actually have an antique rose version of this one that I prefer, but I was never able to make a full-quality version of that one. I love antique roses, ever since Zero and MeMe introduced me to them. MeMe's place was a shelter to quite a few of us street kids and the antique roses she gardened meant her backyard was always full of colors and lovely smells. She had red rose, also, in fact they climbed up a white fence she'd created specifically for them. I love that the rose bites back, that she has thorns and is far from afraid to use them. But then again, I love dangerous and violent women. Why wouldn't I be pulled towards her petals only to find that there were thorns hiding in waiting? _It's why she calls to me._

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/32668480)\]

## The Butterfly Lily

_aka, "UV Lily"_

One of my best sellers and multi-featured across different groups who love art with flowers. I was able to bring out a split-paper effect in her petals, which really gives them this beautiful feeling of movement around her jeweled heart. Then the garden itself is also peppered with more jewels, yet barely straying from the JuliaN form. And if you step back from it and look at a distance... you can almost see Gaston Julia's original equations in her form. .. years before he even took on Mandelbrot as a student. The Julia Set is now a part of the Mandelbrot Set itself, yet the original holds this jagged seed-like quality that I've always loved for its own inner beauty. To be able to draw it out of this lovely flower and bring them together in such a subtle way was no small feat, yet now we all get to bask in her midnight glory.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/32861468)\]

## The Water Lily

In my opinion, this is my finest work on the inner "jewel bud" and I fucking loooooooovveee the radial webbed patterns around the jewel that bloom outward into the petals. For the few who were invited into the walls of "The Reliquary" -- my apartment in Vegas -- they saw this design as an glass-like jewelry box. At the same time, it's worth noting that the designs I posted on social media ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/CFpOK_bHvpq/)) were different than this final form that went to Redbubble and other stores. That other design was darker, less detailed, and did not have the physical weight of this final form. I actually had to take the original parameters for the fractal itself, then go over them again in Chaotica to see why it felt so hollow, adding in post-transforms with blue, balancing out the luminance, and with some very slight recoloring for the deepest levels. When I could really "feel" her, and so much better than before, I had her rendered at much greater detail. That finally bloomed days later into the version that you'll now find on Redbubble and my other stores.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/40066385)\]

## Succulence

This is easily the spiritual successor to my big hit "[Cacti Nova](cacti-nova)" and plays on the colors of my favorite cacti -- the saguaro! For those that don't know, saguaro are the tall, thin cacti with little arms held up in the air to flex their muscles.. . the same ones that we put sombreros on along with Christmas lights throughout southern Arizona and New Mexico. _They're our buds!_ While the colors and pattern of "Cacti Nova" were perfectly befitting of a barrel cactus with its orange, green, and splashes of yellow, this design right here is nearly the exact birds-eye-view of the crown of a saguaro and in the perfect colors for it.

I didn't reach my first desert until the winter of 2001. Strange time to fall in love... and yet they'd already grabbed me. I came back later that spring, then again later that summer. Since then, I've accepted that I'm a desert rat at heart and that the sands will always call me back home. The cacti are my silent companions in those barren wastes that I love.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/51888166)\]

## Extended Exploration

If you somehow missed "[Bloom of Fire](bloom-of-fire)" or "[Filigree Floranocte](filigree-floranocte)" then they're easily my most popular flowers, with "[Spring Pines](spring-pines)" and "[Cacti Nova](cacti-nova)" still to-this-day being my big hits among the natural flora fractals that I've created. An assortment of my favorite fractal flora appear in my "[Spectral Iteration](spectral-iteration)" book for fractal art.
